profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Northern Virginia campus, spanning Loudoun County (Ashburn-Shellhorn, Ashburn-Moran, Ashburn Lockridge buildings), Prince William County (Manassas DC1, DC2, DC5), and Sterling (Ashburn 1, Ashburn 2). Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
QTS Manassas DC5 is one building within a planned six-building, 105-acre campus in Prince William County with a published total critical capacity of 190+ MW. This capacity ranks 24th among Virginia's 23 facilities with published megawatt figures, meaning the Manassas campus as a whole exceeds the disclosed capacity of any single mapped facility in the state. The campus represents approximately 14 percent of Virginia's 1,375 MW of published data center capacity drawn from operator specifications.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 190+ MW campus would support roughly 4,750 racks, or about 3,000 to 4,500 high-end accelerators depending on GPU configuration. The actual IT load and density are not published. QTS operates this campus as part of a larger Northern Virginia footprint spanning Loudoun and Prince William counties, placing it within the dominant US region for hyperscale data center deployment.

The facility's certifications and specific tenant suitability are not published. QTS was acquired by Blackstone in August 2021 and operates as a wholesale provider, meaning its capacity serves customers rather than a named operator. Whether this campus's power and cooling are allocated to model training, inference, or other workloads depends on tenant contracts not visible in public specifications.
